title: Base-flat modules over an unramified algebra are flat
statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings and give $S$ an $R$-algebra structure. Assume it is formally unramified (any two $R$-algebra maps from $S$ to an $R$-algebra agreeing modulo a square-zero ideal are equal) and essentially of finite type (a localization of a finitely generated $R$-algebra). Let $M$ be an $S$-module with a compatible $R$-module action, so $(rs)m=r(sm)$. If $M$ is flat over $R$, meaning tensoring injections of $R$-modules with $M$ preserves injectivity, then $M$ is flat over $S$.
